decisions.reason: The statement never identifies p_t with Law(X_t). For X_t=X_0+W_t with X_0~N(0,1), q is the Brownian heat kernel and the unrelated p_t=N(1,1+t) satisfies normalization, Chapman–Kolmogorov, the forward heat equations and the stated analytic assumptions. Its proposed reverse drift (1-x)/(1+T-u) is globally Lipschitz on the finite horizon, so the assumed reverse martingale problem is well posed for every initial law. The actual reverse drift is -x/(1+T-u). More directly, for s<t the displayed Bayes kernel has conditional mean ((1+s)/(1+t))*y+(t-s)/(1+t), whereas E[X_s|X_t=y]=((1+s)/(1+t))*y. Step 1.1 therefore has a false premise. Repaired by explicitly requiring P(X_t in A)=integral_A p_t(x)dx at every time, including zero; all existing conclusions and other hypotheses are retained.
